facts.raw_span: purpuric lesions on her face, elbows, knees, and feet
dusky purpuric macules and patches on her nose, bilateral cheeks, forehead, and left ear
reticulated purpuric macules and patches on her knees, feet, and the extensor surfaces of her arms
skin sloughing off the lesions on her elbows and knees
Hypercalcemia (calcium level, 11.5 mg/dL)
Acute kidney injury (creatinine level, 5.6 mg/dL)
Rouleaux and cryoprotein precipitate on peripheral blood smear
Abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses
Monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis
Elevated serum cryoglobulin levels (cryocrit, 16%)
Negative results for hepatitis, antinuclear antibodies, rheumatoid factor, heparin-induced thrombocytopenia antibodies, and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies
multifocal intravascular fibrinoid material consisting of a mix of cryoglobulins and fibrin thrombi with relatively little vessel wall inflammation

concepts.why: The patient's presentation with purpuric lesions, elevated serum cryoglobulin levels, and multifocal intravascular fibrinoid material is consistent with cryoglobulinemic vasculitis.
The patient's hypercalcemia, abnormal paraprotein band, and monoclonal IgG-κ protein are consistent with multiple myeloma.
The patient's presentation with cryoglobulinemia and abnormal paraprotein band is also consistent with Waldenström's macroglobulinemia.
The patient's presentation with purpuric lesions and skin sloughing is also consistent with polyarteritis nodosa.
The patient's history of chronic kidney disease and acute kidney injury is consistent with this diagnosis.
The patient's hypercalcemia is likely related to their underlying malignancy.

concepts.preferred_label: Renal impairment due to multiple myeloma
concepts.why: The patient's renal impairment is likely related to their multiple myeloma.
The patient's presentation with cryoglobulinemia and renal impairment is consistent with cryoglobulinemic glomerulonephritis.
